description:
Project: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (Reliability Program)

Context and goals
Redwood Inference’s hosted API experiences bursty, highly variable workloads (prompt-length variance, streaming, customer traffic spikes) where overload can cascade into tail-latency blowups, elevated 5xx rates, and noisy-neighbor effects. This project adds explicit overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) to keep the platform within SLOs and degrade safely when capacity or downstream dependencies are saturated.

Primary goals
- Prevent overload cascades by rejecting or degrading traffic early and predictably.
- Provide clear, customer-facing errors with stable semantics (error codes, retry guidance, correlation IDs) instead of ambiguous timeouts/5xx.
- Enable safe degradation modes (fallback routing, reduced features, queued admission) while preserving tenant isolation.
- Reduce incident count and severity for capacity-related and dependency-related failure modes.
- Improve observability and operability: SLO-driven dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and post-incident learnings integrated into tooling.

Scope
In-scope capabilities
- A “hosted circuit breaker” framework in the request path (API gateway/control plane + routing + runtime admission points).
- Load-shedding policies using real-time signals: GPU queue depth, scheduler backlog, token/sec saturation, memory pressure, regional capacity signals, and downstream dependency health.
- Tier-aware and tenant-aware policies (self-serve vs Dedicated vs enterprise Hosted tiers), including per-route/model limits.
- Customer-visible error taxonomy and response payloads (e.g., 429 vs 503, explicit overload error codes, Retry-After guidance).
- Optional graceful degradation modes:
  - Automated fallback to compatible model variants when configured.
  - Disabling non-essential features under duress (e.g., reduce max_tokens cap, limit concurrency for streaming, reduce tool-calling complexity) behind policy flags.
- Rollout plan and guardrails: dark launch metrics, canary by region, progressive enablement, and fast rollback.

Out-of-scope (initially)
- New customer billing/credits policy changes (only usage enforcement hooks needed for overload).
- Full cross-cloud multi-provider capacity brokering beyond existing routing/failover primitives.
- Major SDK API surface redesign (only error handling improvements and docs).

Key stakeholders and teams
- Eng SRE: program ownership, SLO definitions, incident reduction targets, dashboards/alerts, runbooks (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Christine Wong).
- Platform Control Plane + API Gateway: request admission, policy evaluation, tenant/tier controls (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Amara Diallo, Jordan Lee, Cole Summers).
- Smart Routing: fallback routing and regional policy integration (Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Elena Popov, Peter Holtz).
- Serving Runtime Scheduling: runtime-level backpressure integration and queueing behavior (Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Lena Fischer, Omar El-Sayed, Marcus Reed).
- Product (Hosted API + Dedicated): customer experience, error semantics, rollout comms requirements (Nikhil Sharma, Henry Cho, Lauren Bishop).
- DevEx/Docs + Support/CS: documentation updates, known-issues guidance, escalation playbooks.

Timeline (hypothetical, ~10–12 weeks)
Phase 0 (Week 1–2): Requirements + error taxonomy
- Define overload SLO objectives and guardrails.
- Specify error payloads, codes, and client retry behavior.

Phase 1 (Week 3–6): Implementation and dark launch
- Admission control in gateway + policy engine wiring.
- Runtime saturation signals and routing integration.
- Metrics + dashboards + initial alerts.

Phase 2 (Week 7–9): Canary and progressive rollout
- Canary in one region and subset of tenants.
- Tune thresholds; reduce false positives; validate customer impact.

Phase 3 (Week 10–12): General availability + operationalization
- Publish runbooks and support guidance.
- Post-launch review; incident playbook updates; backlog of enhancements.

Constraints and success metrics
- Backwards compatibility: API responses remain JSON-compatible; new error fields are additive.
- Avoid retry storms: consistent Retry-After and guidance; protect downstreams.
- Success metrics: reduced p95/p99 latency under bursts, fewer saturation-related incidents, lower 5xx/timeouts, improved error-budget burn during load tests and real traffic, improved MTTR when overload occurs.

Deliverables
- Confluence: design docs, ADRs, SLO updates, runbooks, customer-facing error guidance.
- GitHub PRs: gateway middleware, policy engine additions, routing fallback hooks, runtime backpressure integration, telemetry.
- Linear: project plan broken into epics and tasks.
- Slack: implementation coordination, oncall threads, incident simulations/game day.
- Drive: working docs (threshold tuning sheets, load-test plans, rollout checklists).
- Jira: support tickets for early customers seeing overload errors; internal support for dashboards/alerts access.
- GTM/Support enablement: known issues/workarounds and escalation flow updates.

files.description: Program overview: motivations, target failure modes, high-level architecture, phased rollout plan, ownership, and success metrics tied to SLO/error budgets.
ADR defining customer-facing overload error codes, HTTP status mapping, JSON payload shape, Retry-After semantics, and compatibility considerations.
ADR describing where circuit breakers live (gateway vs routing vs runtime), responsibilities, and how signals flow without creating feedback loops.
Platform doc: how overload policies are represented, validated, stored, and evaluated; includes examples of tier/tenant/model-specific rules.
Dashboard spec: key metrics (shed rate, breaker open rate, queue depth, saturation indicators), recommended views, and alert thresholds.
Runtime architecture notes on saturation signals (prefill/decode queue, KV cache pressure, memory fragmentation proxies) and how they’re exported.
Runbook: steps to triage runtime overload, interpret saturation metrics, and apply mitigations (throttle, disable features, adjust batching caps).
SLO update: how overload-induced errors are categorized, what counts toward availability/error budgets, and how to report to customers.
Oncall runbook for circuit breaker incidents: detection, verification, safe toggles, rollback steps, comms templates, and post-incident data capture.
Game day plan: scenarios (burst traffic, dependency brownout, regional capacity dip), success criteria, and roles (incident commander, comms, ops).
Support-facing guidance for new overload errors: how customers should retry/backoff, how to interpret correlation IDs, and when to escalate.
Docs plan and content outline for developer docs: new error codes, recommended client retry policies, idempotency, and example responses.
Working spreadsheet: proposed breaker thresholds per region/model, observed baseline saturation, and tuning notes from load tests.
Draft doc with the JSON schema for overload policies (per-tenant overrides, tier defaults, model/route selectors), plus open questions.
Notes from runtime team: candidate saturation signals, pros/cons, sampling rates, and cardinality concerns.
PM working draft: customer-facing phrasing for overload errors, status page wording, and rollout communication plan.
Observability plan draft: metric names, dimensions to avoid, alert tuning strategy, and example PromQL queries.
Checklist for canary → GA: preconditions, monitoring gates, rollback triggers, support readiness, and launch sign-offs.
Engineering epic: overall work breakdown (gateway admission, routing hooks, runtime signals, metrics), milestones, and dependencies.
Task to implement and validate standardized overload error payloads across gateway and downstream services; links to ADR-014.
Task for API gateway: add request admission middleware with per-tenant/per-route limits and hooks for breaker state.
Task for Smart Routing: support policy-configured fallback models/regions when overload triggers; includes safety constraints.
Task to export runtime saturation signals (queue depth, token/sec saturation, memory pressure proxy) with bounded cardinality.
Task to ship dashboards/alerts and wire into oncall paging; includes false-positive review loop.
PRD for overload protection: customer experience goals, tier policy, SLA considerations, and rollout comms requirements.
PM ticket defining allowed degradation modes (fallback model, feature reduction), required controls, and guardrails.
Task to run a game day and document results; includes scenario scripts, observers, and follow-up bugs.
Task to update SDK/docs examples for handling overload errors (exponential backoff, jitter, respecting Retry-After).
PR in monorepo: introduces standardized overload error response struct, maps internal reasons to stable error codes, adds tests and docs comments.
PR: implements gateway admission control (token bucket + concurrency caps), emits metrics, and integrates policy engine toggles.
PR: adds overload policy rule types, schema validation, and safe defaults; includes migration for existing tenant configs.
PR: routing logic to attempt configured fallback model/region on overload, with loop prevention and bounded retries.
PR: exports runtime scheduling queue depth and saturation gauges, adds aggregation to reduce metric cardinality.
PR: sets Retry-After headers consistently, improves correlation IDs, and adds a short internal “client retry contract” comment block.
PR in observability-pack: new dashboards for shed rate/breaker opens, plus initial alert rules and runbook links.
PR: adds a perf-canary scenario that ramps concurrency/prompt sizes to validate graceful degradation vs timeouts.
PR: incident-bot posts breaker state transitions to #incidents/#eng-oncall with links to dashboards and recommended actions.
PR: SDK improvements to surface overload error codes cleanly, parse Retry-After, and provide an example backoff helper.
PR: adds typed overload error classes and documentation snippets for recommended retry/backoff behavior.
PR: updates SLO toolkit rules to classify overload errors distinctly from 5xx, aligning reporting with updated SLO policy.
Thread coordinating SLO impact: how overload errors should count toward error budget, initial thresholds, and reporting expectations.
Thread on policy schema: per-tenant overrides, default tiers, and guardrails to prevent unsafe configs.
Thread discussing runtime saturation signals: queue depth vs token/sec saturation, sampling rates, and metric cardinality concerns.
Thread debating admission control layering (gateway vs runtime) and failure modes like partial brownouts and retry storms.
Incident thread: burst traffic in us-east causes elevated timeouts; team considers enabling early breaker canary and temporary caps.
Oncall coordination thread: interpreting new breaker metrics, verifying no false positives, and deciding whether to page routing owner.
Support thread: customer asks about new 503 overload response; Support shares draft guidance and asks Eng for canonical explanation.
PM/Eng thread finalizing customer-facing messaging for overload errors and status page wording during canary rollout.
Customer support ticket: reports new overload errors during peak; includes logs, regions, model, and coordination with SRE for threshold tuning.
Ticket from enterprise customer: overload responses lack Retry-After on some routes; links to a GitHub hotfix PR and rollout status.
Customer ticket: configured fallback not taking effect; investigation focuses on routing policy evaluation and loop-prevention logic.
Internal ticket: Support/CS requests access to new overload dashboards and runbooks; includes approvals and RBAC group updates.
Email thread: PM + Eng leaders align on overload error codes, customer wording, and launch timeline; includes attached draft snippet.
Email thread: SRE go/no-go for regional canary, with checklist status, monitoring gates, and rollback criteria.
Transcript: enterprise prospect asks about graceful degradation, Retry-After semantics, and how Redwood prevents noisy-neighbor impacts; includes next steps.
CRM company record: security-sensitive prospect evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated; notes emphasize SLA expectations and explicit overload behavior requirements.
CRM company record: mid-market customer with spiky traffic; notes track incidents/timeouts and interest in overload protection + fallback routing.
CRM company record: evaluation-stage prospect; requirements include clear 429/503 semantics, client retry guidance, and region failover behavior.
